decision_titles: 20% of FY27 allocation set aside for Council Sponsored Programming
plain_text:
Methuen Cultural Council 2026   
   
Ellen Baranowski - Chair  
Olivia Chung - Member 
Taana Latu -Member   
Luis Sanchez - Member  
Carey Smith- Member   
Catherine Zembruski – Member  
  
 
  
Meeting Minutes 
Monday, October 19, 2026 at 6:30 PM 
     Location:  Nevins Memorial Library, Study Room  
1 Call to Order/Roll Call/Vote to Accept Agenda/Public Participation 
The meeting commenced at 6:30 PM.  In attendance were:  Ellen Baranowski, Olivia Chung, 
Taana Latu, Luis Sanchez, Carey Smith, Catherine Zembruski.  No public participation.  Motion to 
accept the agenda: Olivia.  Second: Catherine.  Vote: 6 yes; passed unanimously.       
 
2 Reading and Approval of Minutes- September 14, 2026 meeting  
Motion to approve the minutes: Catherine. Second: Olivia.  Vote: 6 yes; passed unanimously. 
                         
3 Financial Report- Update    
Ellen presented the new FY27 budget.  She made a motion to put 20% of the allocation aside for 
Council Sponsored Programming.  Second: Carey.  Vote: 6 yes; passed unanimously.   
During this cycle, the council will be working with $43,919 (with the official allocation $40,600.)   
Of those funds 
20% will be put aside for Council Sponsored Programming: ($8120)  
5% for Administrative Costs: ($2030)   
The remainder will be for FY27 Grants ($33,769)   
                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
4 Unfinished Council Business   None  
                                                                                                                     
5 New Council Business 
Methuen Day Feedback and Surveys 
Olivia presented the survey data.  27 respondents.  There was discussion about the data results.  
The highest percentages for “what people want funded” went to:  live music/concerts;  literary 
events, readings and story-telling;  and festivals, public art and community events.  Those results 
will help to inform the projects that will be granted this round.  The question about how people 
learn about council-sponsored events indicated that folks follow Facebook and other social 
media sites, Nevins Memorial Library website and public postings, as well as other media sites.
Begin looking at FY27 Grants to start the process of voting 
The group started looking at the 60 submissions for projects and we were able to get through 
phase I of voting… which is to say that we divided projects into 3 categories:  ‘yes’ (projects meet 
our priorities, had a selected venue and exact or approximate date), ‘no’ (projects did not comply 
with priorities, venue and/or date), and ‘maybe’ (projects that need a second look before official 
voting.)   
We determined that 27 projects were ‘yes’ to consider funding or partial funding:   
#s 5, 6, 8, 9, 12, 14, 19, 20, 22, 23, 27, 28, 32, 33, 35, 37, 39, 40, 44, 45, 46, 52, 53 or 54, 55, 58, 59  
22 projects were ‘no: 
#s 2, 4, 10, 11, 13, 16, 21, 25, 29, 30, 31, 36, 38, 41, 42, 43, 47, 48, 50, 51, 56, 60 
and 11 projects were ‘maybe’ and would be looked at again before the vote to consider moving 
them into either the ‘yes’ or ‘no’ categories:   
#s 1, 3, 7, 15, 17, 18, 24, 26, 34, 49, 57 
No voting took place at this meeting.  And any of the first determinations may be reconsidered 
at the next meeting. 
 
6 Engagement and Outreach Subcommittee Report None 
 
7 Announcements/Miscellaneous  At the November meeting, we will look at the possibility of 
adding an emergency meeting to the winter calendar, depending on how far we get with voting. 
Also, at 2027 meeting calendar will be prepared for approval. 
   
8 Adjourn 7:40 PM.  Motion to adjourn: Olivia. Second: Taana.  Vote: 6 yes.  Passed unanimously.   
                                                                         
 
 
Next Regular Meeting:  November 9, 2026; 6:30 PM
